newsitem.title: FRANCE: Esso France says strike slows output at Fos.
newsitem.headline: Esso France says strike slows output at Fos.

text.p: A strike over job cuts slowed down production at French Esso's Fos refinery near Marseille on Tuesday, an Esso spokesman said.
"We have had some slowdown in production but it's certainly not running at a minimum level," he said.
Fos has a capacity of 110,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Esso's 150,000 bpd Port Jerome refinery was unaffected, the spokesman said.
Disruption at Fos was caused by workers joining a one-day strike or go-slow at several plants over oil industry plans to cut jobs. Esso France announced its own job cuts last month.

The Esso spokesman said the strike started at 0400 GMT and was due to last until 2000 GMT. He said not all workers were taking part. The CGT trade union said 90 percent of shift workers and 30 percent of day workers had joined the action.
Unions have said they plan disruption at Port Jerome in northern France between Thursday and Friday.
Esso France is a subsidiary of Exxon Corp.
